The two retail-empty callbacks fill handler-table slots that the engine calls with arguments: a moby update, camera setup/update/exit (one pointer) and a camera priority check (two pointers, int result). Declared with unspecified parameters, their empty copies would be `()` functions and each table call would trap on its signature. They are given the widest shape the tables use; the table initialisers are data, so the slot types are unaffected.

prototypes.why: Recovered callers declare it 20 ways (void or s32 result, with or without the parameter). WebAssembly needs one signature per function; no caller uses the result.

prototypes.label: FUN_00120478
prototypes.why: libgcc's float-to-double conversion. Half the callers declare the result as int (the EE returns the double's bits in $v0); every call site passes it straight to a debug print. One signature is required, and the value is a double.

prototypes.label: FUN_001f98d0
prototypes.why: Assembly-only copy helper (ported in ee-helpers.c). Several callers declare it with unspecified parameters or an s32 result; an unprototyped call compiles to an indirect call whose signature differs from the definition and traps. No caller reads a result.

empty_functions.label: FUN_001e93e8
empty_functions.why: Retail body is `jr ra; nop`: a debug hook compiled out. Recovered callers pass it different argument lists, which one WebAssembly function cannot accept, so each file gets its own empty static copy with the prototype it declares.

empty_functions.label: FUN_001e9448
empty_functions.why: Retail body is `jr ra; daddu v0, zero, zero`: returns 0. Same treatment.

signatures.label: FUN_L00_001f2868
signatures.why: collect_mobies_in_sphere: hand-written EE/VU0 assembly with no C definition. Decoded register use: $a0 the sphere centre (lqc2 vf31, 0($a0)), $a1 a flag mask (kept in $s3, tested with andi 4), $a2 a moby to skip (kept in $s2, compared with each candidate), $a3 kept in $s5, $f12 the radius (mfc1 at 0x1f2884); the count of mobys found returns in $v0 and the list is written at D_L00_00177F00. Recovered callers list the float in different positions, which the EE ignores (floats travel in $f12); in WebAssembly each order is a different signature. This order is the register order.
